fields.h1: Build a Client Onboarding Workflow From Handoff to Day 30
fields.hero_description: Build a client onboarding workflow that gives each new client an owner and logs every step in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: The Parts of a Client Onboarding Workflow
fields.features_subheading: Every new client gets one record that holds its owner and the date each step is due.
fields.feature_1:
A record the moment a deal closes

The app reads your CRM through its API and opens an onboarding record when a deal is marked won. The record carries the contract value and the notes sales left on the deal.
fields.feature_2:
A checklist that fits the service sold

A bookkeeping client and a payroll client need different steps. Tell Emergent which steps belong to which service, and each new record starts with the right checklist.
fields.feature_3:
Requests that chase themselves

Each requested file or login has a due date. The app sends the client a reminder by email on the days you pick, and tells the owner in Slack the day an item runs late.
fields.feature_4:
AI that reads what clients upload

An AI step turns uploaded bank statements and signed forms into fields such as the account number and the start date. A person confirms any field the AI is unsure of.
fields.feature_5:
One board for every client in flight

A live board lists each client by stage and owner, with late items on top. Account leads see which kickoffs are booked and which clients are still waiting on access.
fields.feature_6:
The app's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of your onboarding app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Your team can review how client files are stored and change the app like any other code.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Points Where Client Onboarding Stalls
fields.tab_content_1:
Kickoff lands on day 3 after the deal closes

Tarrant Bay Logistics signs a $36,000 annual plan with Quillhaven Software, and the deal moves to closed won in HubSpot. The app opens an onboarding record with the sales notes and assigns Imogen Saltash, the West region's customer success manager. Kickoff is due within 5 business days and is booked for day 3.
fields.tab_content_2:
Three missing documents reach the partner on day 10

Penhallow Reyes CPA asks each new bookkeeping client for 12 documents, and Fenwright Ceramics has uploaded 9. Odalys Fenwright is emailed every 3 days about the other 3: payroll reports, a loan statement, and a merchant statement. On day 10, the partner, Caspian Moorehouse, gets a direct message listing them.
fields.tab_content_3:
No kickoff until all 4 access grants land

Larkspire Media needs 4 accounts shared before it starts work for Hollin Grove Dental: ads, analytics, social, and the website editor. Three of the 4 are granted, and the social account has been pending for 2 days. The office manager, Rosalind Achterberg, gets a reminder with the steps, and the kickoff stays on hold.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any check-in score under 3 reaches the account lead

On day 30 after go-live, Corrigan Peak IT asks Silverbeck Architects 3 questions. The office manager, Pieter Lindqvist, rates setup as promised at 2 out of 5 and writes that two laptops still lack the shared drive. Any score under 3 goes to the account lead, and Marisol Thackeray has a direct message with his comment.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Client Onboarding Workflow
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a client onboarding workflow with owners and deadlines, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Map the stages after the deal closes
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Pick the event that opens a record
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the reminder and escalation days
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each stage between the signed contract and the first piece of delivered work, starting with the sales handoff and ending with the first check-in. Next to each stage, note who owns it today and what it waits on.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List the items each service needs before work can start, and give each item an owner on your side or the client's. Keep them separate per service, because a bookkeeping client and an ad campaign client wait on different things.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose the one event that starts onboarding, such as a deal marked won in your CRM or a signed contract. Opening the record from that event means no new client depends on someone remembering to set it up by hand.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide two numbers per item: how often the client gets a reminder, and how many days late it can run before your account lead or a partner hears about it. Put the kickoff deadline in the same place.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the workflow in a prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the checklists and day counts in plain English, the way you would brief a new hire. Emergent builds the onboarding app from that prompt: the client record, the reminders, the client upload page, and the board.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect the tools you already use
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect the tools the workflow reads from and writes to through their APIs, such as HubSpot for closed deals, your email for client reminders, and Slack for alerts to your team. Each new client then arrives with its deal details filled in.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before a real client sees it, replay three recent onboardings in the app with their real dates. Check that each reminder would have gone out on the right day, and fix any step that fired too early or too late.

faq_plan.q: What is a client onboarding workflow?
faq_plan.a: A client onboarding workflow is the set of steps a business runs between a signed deal and a client who is fully set up. Each step has an owner and a due date. Client onboarding is the process of welcoming new clients into your business. The workflow makes that welcome run the same way for every client, whoever closed the deal.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a client onboarding workflow?
faq_plan.a: Start from your last few clients. List each stage they went through, the items you waited on, and who chased them. Turn that into one checklist per service, add the day each reminder goes out, and choose what starts a new record. In Emergent's AI automation builder, you describe all of that in plain English and get a working app.

faq_plan.q: What does a customer onboarding workflow look like for a software company?
faq_plan.a: For a software product, the customer onboarding workflow covers everything between the closed deal and the customer's first real use of the product. Plan for a handoff from sales with the notes, a kickoff call, account setup and data import, and training for the people who log in daily. Thirty days in, check whether those people use it, not only whether the tasks are done.

faq_plan.q: How do you automate a client onboarding workflow without losing the personal touch?
faq_plan.hint: How to automate client onboarding workflows?
faq_plan.a: Automate the chasing and keep the conversations. Reminders and document requests can run on their own. A person runs the kickoff call and answers any unhappy client. Recruitment automation works on the same split: software schedules and reminds, and people interview. Emergent builds the automated half from a plain-English prompt.

faq_plan.q: What are the first steps in a client onboarding workflow?
faq_plan.hint: What are the first steps in the client onboarding workflow?
faq_plan.a: The first step is the handoff from whoever closed the deal: what was promised, to whom, and by when. Send the welcome within one business day, name one point of contact on each side, and ask for everything you need in a single request instead of a string of emails. Book the kickoff in that first message.

faq_plan.q: How long should a client onboarding workflow take?
faq_plan.a: There is no standard length. Set one per service and measure against it. A bookkeeping client can be ready once the documents are in, while a software rollout can run for several weeks. Give each stage its own target, such as a kickoff inside one week of the close, and the slow stage shows itself.

faq_plan.q: When does a client onboarding workflow end and regular support take over?
faq_plan.a: The workflow ends when the client gets the first result they signed up for, not when the checklist is done. Agree on that result at kickoff, such as the first monthly close or the first live campaign. After it, hand the account to your support team on a short call, and route new requests through customer service automation instead of one person's inbox.

faq_plan.q: What documents should a client onboarding workflow collect?
faq_plan.a: Collect only what the first piece of work needs: the signed agreement, billing and contact details, and the files or logins the service runs on. An accounting firm needs statements, and an agency needs account access. Ask once in a single list and let the client upload against each line. Apps built with Emergent keep every file in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do you measure whether a client onboarding workflow is working?
faq_plan.a: Track how many days pass before kickoff and before the first delivery, the open items past due, and the day-30 check-in score. Compare them by service and by account lead, and fix the slowest stage first. An app built with Emergent can show those numbers on a live dashboard that updates as each step closes.

faq_plan.q: Should welcome emails come from the client onboarding workflow or the marketing tool?
faq_plan.a: Send them from the onboarding workflow. A welcome email depends on the client's record, such as their owner and their kickoff link, and the onboarding app holds that record. Keep the marketing automation workflow for prospects and newsletters, and take new clients out of sales sequences on the day the deal closes.

plan.angle: The top 10 are glossary entries and step-list blogs that describe client onboarding but never show it running. This page names the stages from signed deal to the first check-in, then shows the app that runs four of them for four kinds of service business: a software company's sales handoff, an accounting firm's document collection, a marketing agency's access requests, and an IT firm's day-30 check-in. The FAQ covers the first steps, timing, documents, metrics, the support handoff and welcome emails, and leaves question wording to the client onboarding questionnaire page.
